name: Shorabet Adas (Lentil Soup)

ingredients.name: dried red lentils, picked over and rinsed

instructions.primary_message: For the Soup: In a large pot, heat 2 tablespoons olive oil over medium heat until shimmering. Add onion and cook, stirring occasionally, until lightly golden, about 7 minutes. Add cumin and pepper and cook until fragrant, about 30 seconds.
Stir in potatoes, lentils, carrots, stock, and salt. Bring to a boil over medium-high heat. Reduce heat to a simmer. Cook, covered, until potatoes, lentils, and carrots are tender, about 15 minutes.

For the Pita Chips (optional): While soup cooks, line a large plate with paper towels. Heat about 0.5 cm olive oil in a large stainless steel skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering. Working in two batches, add half of pita squares and cook, stirring and flipping pita often, until golden, 2 to 3 minutes, taking care not to let them darken too much. Using a slotted spoon, immediately transfer to prepared plate and season with salt to taste.

Once soup is cooked, transfer lentil mixture to a blender. Blend on medium-high speed until smooth, about 1 minute. (Alternatively, blend soup with an immersion blender until smooth.) Divide soup between serving bowls and top with parsley and pita chips, if using. Serve with lemon wedges on the side.

schema_metadata.keywords: lentil soup, vegetable soup, puréed soup, puréed lentil soup

description: In this satisfying 30-minute lentil soup, red lentils are simmered with onion, potatoes, carrots, and cumin, then blended until creamy and served with lemon wedges and pita chips.
notes:
Optional or for serving: Large lemon wedges, for serving (see notes); Chopped parsley, for serving

Optional substitutions: unsalted chicken stock → vegetable stock

Notes: Serve with plenty of large lemon wedges—shorabet adas is meant to be bright and lemon-forward.
While chicken stock adds savoriness to the soup, vegetable stock works well for a vegan version.

Make-ahead and storage: Leftovers can be refrigerated in an airtight container for up to 4 days.
author: Laila Ibrahim
